sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Funds should be allocated keeping in mind total income. (ii) Family income includes money from salary, rent and bank interest only. (iii) Cost of living is more in big cities. (iv) Expenditure should be less than income to save.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – it also includes savings from using skills and free facilities. (iii) True. (iv) True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) A budget is the process of allocating income among various uses. (ii) A budget cannot help in achieving long-term goals. (iii) Income of family members does not influence the budget. (iv) The main purpose of a budget is to live within income.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – it can help. (iii) False – it does. (iv) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Whatever comes into the family as money is ______. (ii) Money set aside for the future is ______. (iii) Expenditure > income leads to ______. (iv) About ______ % of income should be saved.

Match the factor with its effect on expenditure: (i) Size of family (ii) Age of members (iii) Place of residence (iv) Skills of members; (a) higher cost of living in big cities (b) fewer repair bills (c) more on food and clothing (d) more on education.
Match the expense with its budget head: (i) Repair of a tap (ii) Bus fare to a friend's house (iii) Electricity bill (iv) Eating out; (a) public utility (b) entertainment (c) house (d) transport.
Arrange the steps of making a spending plan: (a) allocate funds (b) list all requirements (c) balance the plan (d) prioritise needs (e) keep in mind income and facilities.

State True or False: (i) Using free medical facilities saves money. (ii) A budget forces you to decide what is more important. (iii) A major part of the income is spent on food. (iv) Records of expenditure help to control unnecessary expenses.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Families are not able to meet their needs with rising inflation. Suggest four ways to cut their expenses.
questions.answer: Avoid wasting food and eating out; save electricity and water; use public transport or a cycle; iron and wash clothes at home; use stationery economically; borrow from the public library; look out for sales and shop in one trip; avoid impulsive buying.

or.q: Prepare a format to record one month food expenses of your family.
or.answer: A table headed Month and Year with rows for cereals, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk, ghee/oil, spices, egg/meat and others, columns for Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 and Week 4, and a Total column for each item and for the month.

questions.q: Give four suggestions to your newly-wed sister to save money to go for a holiday.
questions.answer: Make a monthly spending plan and fix a saving amount; cut down eating out; avoid impulsive buying; use public transport; save electricity; keep records of expenses; earn extra money with her skills.

questions.q: Gurdip studies in college and wants to become financially independent. Suggest four ways he can supplement his family income.
questions.answer: Take tuitions; do part-time work or typing; stitch or repair household gadgets; make handicrafts or preserved foods for sale; grow vegetables at home; work during vacations.

questions.q: How can you increase your family income from home?
questions.answer: Use skills like stitching, knitting, tuitions or crèche; start household production such as a kitchen garden, poultry, bee-keeping or preserved foods; sell handicrafts; rent a room or take a paying guest.

questions.q: Other than salary, identify any two sources of family income.
questions.answer: Rent from a house or shop; interest from the bank; profit from investments; part-time earnings; savings from using skills and free facilities.

questions.q: Give any three reasons for saving money.
questions.answer: To meet emergencies and health needs; for children's education and marriage; for old age security; to buy household goods or a house.

questions.q: What is a spending plan? Write any two of its advantages.
questions.answer: A spending plan (budget) is a planned approach to spending money based on the total income of the family. It helps the family live within its income, save for future needs and emergencies, and avoid impulsive buying.

questions.q: Why should a record of expenditure be maintained? Give any four reasons.
questions.answer: To know how much was spent on each item; to compare with the previous month; to control unnecessary expenses; to plan for the future; to save money; to compare old and new prices; to avoid being cheated.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Mr Gupta lives in his own house with his children aged 17 and 20 years. He earns Rs 38,000 a month. Prepare a spending plan for his family.
questions.answer: Using the guide percentages on Rs 38,000: food 35% = 38,000 x 35/100 = Rs 13,300; housing (repairs, taxes, utilities) 20% = Rs 7,600; clothing 5% = Rs 1,900; recreation 5% = Rs 1,900; household operations 6% = Rs 2,280; education 5% = Rs 1,900; transport 8% = Rs 3,040; medical 3% = Rs 1,140; furnishing 3% = Rs 1,140; savings 10% = Rs 3,800. Total = 13,300 + 7,600 + 1,900 + 1,900 + 2,280 + 1,900 + 3,040 + 1,140 + 1,140 + 3,800 = Rs 38,000, so the plan is balanced. (Education may be raised a little by trimming recreation.)

questions.q: Prepare a spending plan for a family with a monthly income of Rs 31,000 using the guide percentages.
questions.answer: Food 35% = Rs 10,850; housing 20% = Rs 6,200; clothing 5% = Rs 1,550; recreation 5% = Rs 1,550; household operations 6% = Rs 1,860; education 5% = Rs 1,550; transport 8% = Rs 2,480; medical 3% = Rs 930; furnishing 3% = Rs 930; savings 10% = Rs 3,100. Total = 10,850 + 6,200 + 1,550 + 1,550 + 1,860 + 1,550 + 2,480 + 930 + 930 + 3,100 = Rs 31,000.

questions.q: Sonali cannot meet her monthly expenses with her present income. Suggest ways to balance her spending plan.
questions.answer: She can earn more (tuitions, stitching, handicrafts, a part-time job, kitchen garden or preserved foods) or cut down expenses (avoid food waste and eating out, save electricity and water, use public transport, iron and wash at home, use the public library, buy during sales, avoid impulsive buying, and allot funds to unnecessary items last).

questions.q: List the characteristics of a good budget.
questions.answer: It has accurate estimates of income (gross income differs from take-home pay); accurate estimates of expenditure based on past records; reasonably accurate allocation that anticipates festivals and future changes; and it is flexible, with a margin so money can be moved from one item to another.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps of making a spending plan and the factors on which allocation of money to different items depends.
questions.answer: Steps: keep in mind all income and facilities; list all requirements; prioritise needs; allocate funds according to total income; balance the plan (earn more or cut expenses) and keep records. Allocation depends on income of the family, size of the family, age of family members (school-going children), place of residence (cost of living is higher in big cities), skills of members and the amount to be saved (about 10%).

questions.q: Write five points highlighting the importance of a family spending plan.
questions.answer: (1) It helps the family live within its income. (2) It helps to save money for future needs and emergencies. (3) It avoids borrowing. (4) It discourages impulsive buying. (5) It helps to meet all needs of all family members by listing and prioritising them. (6) Records help to control unnecessary expenses and avoid being cheated.
